games.film: Ole Miss goes as Trinidad Chambliss goes. If you squeeze his pocket and take away his downfield shots, their offense stalls. Defensively, their front can be bullied with a powerful run game, and their secondary can be picked apart if caught in space. Stay home on Chambliss, cap the shot plays, and run the front.
filmNotes: Ole Miss is no-huddle shotgun and Trinidad Chambliss. Ole Miss goes as Trinidad Chambliss goes. If you squeeze his pocket and take away his downfield shots, their offense stalls. Defensively, their front can be bullied with a powerful run game, and their secondary can be picked apart if caught in space. Stay home on Chambliss, cap the shot plays, and run the front.
Schematic Identity: Pure no-huddle, shotgun-only attack. High-velocity tempo designed to score quickly rather than bleed the clock (TOP: 27:11).
Efficiency Metrics: Averaging 38.0 PPG and 445.0 YPG (331.0 pass / 114.0 rush).
Situational Success: Highly efficient on money downs (46% 3rd Down) and aggressive on 4th-and-short (2-for-3). Lethal inside the 20, going 12-for-12 in the Red Zone with 11 touchdowns.

QB Trinidad Chambliss: The engine of the offense. Stat line: 70% (77-of-110), 924 yards, 7 TD, 2 INT. Will sit comfortably in the pocket to execute isolated vertical shots, but lethal when breaking structure. Threw a brilliant 20-yard back-corner TD on the run to Deuce Alexander vs. LSU. In tight situational moments, they default to the QB Keep (scored from 14 yards out to break a 24–24 tie). Flaws: Susceptible to holding the ball too long (took a 20-yard sack vs. LSU) and will throw interceptions if forced into late, past-the-downfield-read progressions.

Wide Receivers: Deep, balanced group where defenses cannot isolate or bracket a single target. Four wideouts cleared 50 yards against LSU. Traylon Ray: The primary vertical and isolated X-receiver boundary threat. Posted a 7-115-1 line vs. LSU, including a 21-yard play-action score over the top. Deuce Alexander: The high-volume chain-mover and scramble-drill target. Exploded for two 62-yard plays vs. Louisville; followed up with 7-60-1 vs. LSU. Caleb Odom & Horatio Fields: Intermediary, middle-of-the-field threats. Logged 5-88 and 5-52 respectively against LSU.

Ground Game: Secondary component to the passing attack. Kewan Lacy: Primary early-down and short-yardage back (39 carries, 191 yards, 4 TD). Suffered a shoulder injury against LSU; his status is a game-time decision. JT Lindsey: Next man up if Lacy scratches. Logged 4 carries for 20 yards vs. LSU, executing a critical 4th-and-1 sneak and a 2-point conversion.

Schematic Identity: Pete Golding calls a Base 4-2-5 alignment (4 down linemen, 2 linebackers, 5 defensive backs). Heavy emphasis on pre-snap disguise and defensive back versatility. (e.g., Jaylon Braxton rotated dynamically between safety and corner against LSU).

Front Seven: Excellent pursuit speed, but lacks physical consistency against downhill run schemes. Stressed heavily by combo blocks and space assignments, yielding 162 rushing yards to Louisville and 172 rushing yards to LSU (Dilin Jones individual: 106 yards). Will Echoles: Stout interior anchor (6-3, 315 lbs) capable of collapsing pockets. Blake Purchase: Primary edge threat with closing speed. Tah'j Butler, Luke Ferrelli, Keaton Thomas: Main off-ball tacklers; highly active but can get caught on blocks. Suntarine Perkins: The defensive wildcard. Functions as a hybrid chess piece utilized for edge rushing, delayed blitzes, or zone drops.

Secondary: Proven ability to close games in high-leverage moments. Kam Franklin tipped a crucial 4th-and-goal pass that Jaylon Braxton intercepted to seal the LSU win. Sharif Denson excelled in his debut against LSU with 8 tackles. Flaws: Susceptible to coverage lapses and communication issues when stressed horizontally in space (Louisville threw for 307 yards).

Kicker Lucas Carneiro: 5-for-7 on field goals this season. Displays range but lacks elite consistency (hit from 37, missed from 53), though he converted a clutch 48-yard walk-off winner against Louisville.
